children.text: Bayambang Church is the Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church, a parish said to date from 1619. Pair it with the St. Vincent Ferrer Prayer Park, home to a 50.23 m bamboo statue completed in 2019, for an easy day-trip pilgrimage.

Bayambang is the southernmost town in Pangasinan, set on the broad plains along the Agno River. It borders Tarlac Province, and Wikipedia describes it as a gateway into Pangasinan. The church's official name is the Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church. It lies about
180km
in a straight line from Manila, so an early start makes a day trip possible.

Several records trace the parish to 1619. It is said to have been founded by Dominican missionaries, and the parish held its 400th anniversary celebrations in April 2019. The dates for how the building came to stand on its present site vary from record to record. A history published in the town's municipal news says that after floods in 1741, residents of Malunguey moved to the present site, and the wooden church and convent were moved with them. The change to a stone church then went through repeated fires and earthquakes. According to the same account, a fire in 1856 badly damaged the church and convent, after which the walls were rebuilt with cut square stone from a quarry across the Agno River and topped with a tile roof. The 1863 earthquake then badly damaged the tile roof. Wikipedia says a second church and convent of stone and mortar with a galvanized iron roof were built in 1869. The July 1990 Luzon earthquake also damaged the ceiling and façade; during repairs the old wooden ceiling was replaced with plywood and the cement was scraped off the walls, exposing the stone beneath.

The façade has two levels, with six Ionic columns and statue niches in the pediment. The bell tower on the left is a later addition, so its style differs slightly from the façade. Behind the central altar, the main retablo holds a statue of St. Vincent Ferrer, and the saint's relic is said to be kept at the foot of the statue. In 2001 the roof and paintwork were extensively repaired, and in 2006 the retablo and tabernacle were refurbished and eight large chandeliers were added. In 2013–2014 the sanctuary received granite tiles and iron grills, along with new pews and stained glass. The church you see today is the product of repairs from many eras, so it is fun to tell the old stone walls apart from the newer fittings.

Another reason visitors come to Bayambang today is the St. Vincent Ferrer Prayer Park, which opened in 2019. A 50.23 m statue of the saint, built by cladding a steel frame in engineered bamboo, stands here. Guinness World Records recognizes it as the tallest supported bamboo sculpture in the world. Seeing the church and the bamboo statue together makes for a day that combines an old place of faith with a modern monument.

This is a church whose parish is said to have been started by the Dominicans in 1619. The thick stone walls and the façade with Ionic columns give it the feel of an old Spanish-era church. It has been reported that the church was elevated to an archdiocesan shrine on April 5, 2025, so check current local information.

blocks.title: The relic and the central altar

children.text: St. Vincent Ferrer's relic is said to be enshrined at the foot of the saint's statue on the main retablo above the central altar. Even non-believers can walk quietly toward the altar, but during Mass it is polite to stay near the back so as not to disturb worshippers.

The two-level façade, the six Ionic columns and the pediment niches are the main things to look at. Records say the bell tower on the left was built anew in concrete and blessed in 1974, which helps explain why its style differs from the façade.

The statue at the St. Vincent Ferrer Prayer Park is 50.23 m tall in total, with the figure of the saint itself about 42 m. It is covered with about 22,626 bamboo panels, and the bamboo, about 60 tons, was reportedly imported from China. It is visible from far away, which makes it great for photos.

The park is described as having a chapel, gardens and Stations of the Cross placed along its paths. One description says the park stands on high ground overlooking open farmland, with lovely views at dusk. Opening hours differ by source, so check before you go.

blocks.title: The story of the bomb that did not explode

children.text: During World War II a bomb fell inside the church nave and did not explode, which locals tell as a miracle of St. Vincent Ferrer. The story appears in the church history published in the town's municipal news, and it is easier to follow alongside the record that the church roof was heavily damaged during the war.

blocks.title: Parish feast in April and the Malangsi festival

children.text: St. Vincent Ferrer's feast day is April 5. In the first week of April, around the same time, the Malangsi Fish Festival takes place, and on April 5, 2014 the town set a Guinness record for the longest barbecue grill. Crowds gather during the festival, so check the schedule and transport in advance.

items.title: Half-day route
items.subtitle: The church and the prayer park

children.text: Take a northbound bus from the Pasay, Cubao or Caloocan terminals in Manila. Before boarding, confirm whether the Pangasinan-bound bus passes through Bayambang; if not, transfer at Tarlac City or Dagupan.

Arrive in Bayambang town and head to Saint Vincent Ferrer Parish Church. View the façade and bell tower from outside first, then step inside at a time when no Mass is being held and look around the central altar and the statue quietly.
Have lunch in the plaza area beside the church or in town. Fish buro, a fermented fish condiment, is said to be a local specialty, but check that it suits your taste first.
Go by tricycle or private car to the St. Vincent Ferrer Prayer Park in Barangay Bani. The coordinates of the church and the park are roughly 2 km apart in a straight line.
Look up at the bamboo statue and walk through the park's gardens, chapel and Stations of the Cross. The midday hours are very hot, so rest in shaded spots as you go.
Return to town and continue to Manila or your next destination. Evening bus frequency may drop, so settle your return transport in advance.

Since the route covers only the church and the park, half a day is enough even at a relaxed pace. You can also combine it with Lingayen in northern Pangasinan or Manaoag Church for a two-day pilgrimage. Around the town plaza, look out for historical markers or monuments. Bayambang is described as having served briefly in 1899 as the fifth capital of the First Philippine Republic, so there is plenty of history beyond the church.

items.title: By bus from Manila, with a transfer

children.text: Bayambang is about
180km
from Manila. Buses toward Pangasinan leave from Pasay, Cubao and Caloocan, and regular Victory Liner fares to Dagupan are reported at about
(figures differ by source).
Route-planning services suggest a way from Manila to Bayambang via Tarlac and estimate roughly 5 hours. Depending on traffic and transfers, it can take closer to 6 hours.

I could not confirm which bus companies and routes stop directly in Bayambang. Ask terminal staff whether the bus stops in Bayambang or whether you should transfer at Tarlac City, and decide from there.
Bus fares and timetables change often. Check the latest notices and terminal information.

items.title: By private car or rental car

children.text: The usual way is to head north from Manila on the SCTEX and TPLEX expressways toward Tarlac, then continue into Bayambang. Check the exact exit and arrival time on a map app.
The church and the prayer park are a short distance apart, so having your own car makes getting around easy.
In Bayambang town you can walk between the church and the plaza, and use a tricycle or private car to reach the prayer park.
Tricycle fares must be negotiated, so state your destination and whether you want a round trip before boarding, and agree on a price.
The dry season in central Luzon, from November to May, is a good time to visit. Because the route involves walking outdoors in the prayer park, the drier months are more comfortable.
Around the April 5 parish feast the town is crowded, as it overlaps with the Malangsi Fish Festival. This is a good time if you want to enjoy the events, but be ready for traffic and crowds.

Many people visit Bayambang as a day trip. You can use a small guesthouse in town, but size and price must be confirmed locally. Another option is to stay in Lingayen in northern Pangasinan or in a nearby city.

You will take meals at restaurants and shops in town. Bayambang is said to be famous for buro, a fermented fish condiment, and during festivals grilled fish over charcoal fills the streets. If it is your first time, the smell and taste can be strong, so start with a small amount.
Keep quiet inside the church so as not to disturb Mass and prayer, and refrain from taking photos when many worshippers are present.
Modest clothing that covers the knees and shoulders is best.
The church and the prayer park are about 2 km apart, so decide on your transport in advance if you want to see both in one day.
The bamboo statue area is very hot in the daytime. Bring a hat, sunscreen and water.
Around the April 5 parish feast the town is busy with events. If you want photos on that day, arrive early.
Bus services vary by season, so confirm the time of the last bus back locally.
Access may be restricted by church repairs or events. Check the latest notices.
Some local information lacks an official announcement from the operator, so look for guidance from the parish or the town hall before you go.

The church is still a place of faith where Mass is held. During services worship takes priority over sightseeing, and the prayer park's opening hours and fees are hard to confirm officially, so check before you visit.
The founding year and building history of the church differ between records, so it is hard to be definitive. Give priority to signs and local explanations.
Information about direct buses is scarce. A transfer may be needed, so allow extra time.
Daytime temperatures are high and some places have little shade, so watch out for heatstroke.
In the rainy season, heavy rain can make roads difficult.
Take the usual care of your belongings, including against pickpockets.
This place explores the history and art sights of downtown Tarlac, and it is also a city where you may transfer on the way from Manila. It is close to Bayambang and easy to combine.
One of the main pilgrimage sites of Tarlac, which can be combined with Bayambang on the same route.
